findings.title: Real-world experiments early-stop and pick the checkpoint on the TEST set
findings.claim: In the real-world runner, `trainer.fit` receives the TEST dataloader as `val_dataloaders`; the `EarlyStopping` and `ModelCheckpoint` callbacks both monitor `val_{loss}` (run_realworld.py:170,178), so the reported checkpoint is the epoch that minimises the loss on the test set, which is then re-used as the final test metric (line 212).
findings.concern: Every real-world number (Tab. 1 and Tab. 2) is an optimistic best-epoch-on-test estimate — model selection is performed on the same data used for evaluation — even though the configs define a separate validation split (la/bay `val_len: 0.1`, engrad `val_len: 2016`) that `dm.val_dataloader()` exposes but the code never uses.
findings.resolution: Re-run with `val_dataloaders=dm.val_dataloader()` (the 10%/2016-step validation split the paper's Appendix B describes) for early stopping and checkpointing, then report the untouched test set; quantify the gap vs the current test-selected numbers.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix B ('70%/10%/20% partitions for training, validation, and testing'); Tab. 1; Tab. 2
findings.reason: Lines 200-202 confirm `val_dataloaders=dm.test_dataloader()` and lines 170/178 confirm EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint both monitor `val_{cfg.loss_fn.lower()}`, exactly as claimed.

findings.title: mptcn_diff (the real-world model) binds GCNConv, not the Diffusion Convolution
findings.claim: `DiffConvMixin` (mixed into `MPTCN_DiffConvModel`, i.e. model name `mptcn_diff`, the default MP model for every real-world run per `config/realworld.yaml`) sets `gnn_class = GCNConv`, byte-identical to `GCNMixin`; the `DiffConv` symbol imported on line 3 is never used as a value (`_audit_code/out/diffconv_is_gcn.json`: `DiffConv_used_as_value=false`).
findings.concern: The paper states the MP layer is 'the Diffusion Convolution operator from [54] ... different weights from both incoming and outgoing neighbors up to 2 hops' (Sec. 5.1 / Appendix B), but the executed operator is a symmetric, self-looped, 1-hop GCN, so Tab. 1/Tab. 2 MPTCN numbers and Tab. 2's 'w/ DCNN' column were not produced by the described architecture.
findings.resolution: Confirm whether Tab. 1/2 used DCNN or GCN; if DCNN was intended, set `gnn_class = DiffConv` with the k=2 bidirectional kwargs and re-run, or correct the paper to state GCN.
findings.paper_ref: Sec. 5.1 'features the Diffusion Convolution (DCNN) operator [54] as the MP layer'; Appendix B 'Baselines'; Tab. 2
findings.reason: Lines 26-33 of gnn_mixin.py confirm that DiffConvMixin sets gnn_class = GCNConv (identical to GCNMixin), and DiffConv is imported on line 3 but never assigned as a class attribute.

findings.title: No FOSR rewiring and no RGCN model anywhere in the repo (Table 2 unreproducible)
findings.claim: The model registry offers only GCN/GraphConv/DiffConv-named MPTCNs and GWNet; there is no RGCN model, and a repo-wide search finds zero occurrences of `fosr`, `rewir`, or `rgcn` (`_audit_code/out/missing_components.json`).
findings.concern: Table 2 ('FOSR rewiring' × {RGCN, DCNN}, with/without row-normalization on EngRAD) — which supports the paper's contribution that combining spatial and temporal rewiring mitigates over-squashing — cannot be reproduced because neither the FOSR rewiring step nor the RGCN model exists in the code.
findings.resolution: Release the FOSR-rewiring preprocessing and the RGCN model configuration used for Table 2, or point to where they live.
findings.paper_ref: Tab. 2 and 'Combining spatial and temporal rewiring' (Sec. 5.1)
findings.reason: The model registry quote matches exactly at lines 9-26, and a repo-wide grep for 'fosr', 'rewir', and 'rgcn' returns zero results, confirming their complete absence.

findings.claim: `generate_graph` enumerates identity/ring/crossed_ring/path/lollipop/*_reg/*barbell/community and raises for anything else; there is no 'tree' generator (`_audit_code/out/missing_components.json`: `tree_generator_present=false`). `MemoryTestDataset.generate_y` implements only regression targets (memorize/dump averaging); no classification target, `cross_entropy`, or `accuracy` metric exists anywhere (all counts 0).
findings.concern: Appendix D / Table 5 (TEMPORALTREENEIGHBOURSMATCH: test accuracy on a fixed TREE topology with a match-and-route classification target) cannot be generated or evaluated from the repo — the tree topology and the classification task/metric are both absent.
findings.resolution: Provide the tree-topology generator and the NeighboursMatch classification dataset/metric used for Table 5, or state that this appendix experiment is not included in the release.
findings.reason: Lines 196-203 of syntethic.py confirm the quote exactly — 'community' is the last valid generator before the NotImplementedError, and no 'cross_entropy', 'accuracy', or 'NeighboursMatch' term exists anywhere in the file.

findings.title: No committed config/command reproduces the ROCKETMAN (k,i) success grid
findings.quote: the goal is to copy the average value associated with
findings.claim: The ROCKETMAN building blocks exist (ring/lollipop generators; `MemoryTestDataset` memorize=neighbors), but the config directory contains only `run_copy_time` (Fig. 3) and `run_realworld*` (Tab. 1) drivers, and the word 'rocketman' appears nowhere in the repo (`_audit_code/out/missing_components.json`). The exact configuration that sweeps spatial distance k and temporal distance i to produce the Fig. 4/7 per-cell success rates is not committed.
findings.concern: Figures 4 and 7 (a labelled empirical result central to the T&S vs TTS synthetic validation) are not reproducible from a released command, and how k and i map onto the dataset parameters is left implicit.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add the ROCKETMAN sweep config (graph, N=16, T=9, k/i ranges, #seeds) and the success-rate aggregation used for Figs. 4/7.
findings.reason: The paper (paper_text.txt) confirms ROCKETMAN in Figures 4 and 7 with the quoted phrase present; a repo-wide grep finds zero occurrences of 'rocketman', and the config directory contains only run_copy_time.yaml and run_realworld*.yaml configs, confirming no ROCKETMAN sweep config was committed.
